title: Count feature-flag writes over any map

blocks.text: The config service keeps feature flags in a `Map<String, Boolean>`, and the audit needs to know how many flag writes each deploy made. Flags are written one at a time from the admin UI (`put`) and in batches by the config sync (`putAll`). The store isn't always the same map: production passes a `HashMap`, the nightly report a `TreeMap` so its output is sorted. The audit also compares each snapshot of the flags with the previous one, and keeps the snapshots it has already filed in a `HashSet` so the same one isn't filed twice.

`WriteCountingMap.java` holds a `WriteCountingMap` that wraps whatever map it is given, on top of a `ForwardingMap` that already passes every `Map` method on to that map. Finish the four `TODO` methods, about six lines in total:

items: `WriteCountingMap.put` and `putAll`: `writes()` counts every mapping written through the wrapper, an overwrite of an existing key included, whichever map is underneath;
`ForwardingMap.equals` and `hashCode`: a wrapper compares and hashes like the map it wraps, so the audit's comparisons and its `HashSet` treat it as the flags it holds.

cases.says: every put is one write, an overwrite included, and the map holds the latest values
what is written through the wrapper lands in the map it wraps, and the other way round
a batch written with putAll counts one write per mapping, over a HashMap and over a TreeMap
the wrapper equals a plain map with the same mappings, whichever of the two is asked
a wrapper stored in a HashSet is found by a plain map with the same mappings

origin.section: javac Makes a Forwarding Class Implement Set's Methods, Not equals and hashCode

concepts: javac doesn't make a forwarding class implement equals and hashCode, and without them the wrapper's equality depends on which side is asked and hash lookups miss.
A forwarding wrapper counts each element once over any implementation, because the wrapped object's internal calls stay on the wrapped object.
